It was found by an agent scanning the card's transaction history, identifying a recurring pattern that did not fit any known typology. The affected card was from region 330, and the device used was Trident/7.0, Windows 10, IE 11.0, with a screen resolution of 1920x1080. The exposure amount is $1,289.91.

sar.narrative: Customer C12865, holder of card C12865-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-12-26 14:49 and 2016-12-26 15:11, 3 transaction(s) totalling $1,289.91 were made on the card online from device profile 'Trident/7.0 | Windows 10 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1920x1080': $429.98 (3576364, 2016-12-26 14:49), $429.96 (3576365, 2016-12-26 14:49), $429.97 (3576415, 2016-12-26 15:11). Every amount sat just below $500 and the purchases were placed minutes apart, a pattern consistent with deliberately staying under an authorisation threshold. When contacted, the cardholder stated they did not make the transactions and still holds the card. The activity is suspicious because: 3 online purchases within 22 minutes, each between $400 and $500 ($429.98, $429.96, $429.97; total $1,289.91). It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-3146, CC-4002, CC-0679. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placed linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retains the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.

stop_reason: The requested verification settled it: the cardholder denied the activity, raising the probability to 0.95. Further graph steps would not change the actions (policy 6).
